topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains local tumour treatment and how chemotherapy can support its effectiveness.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how conventional cytotoxic drugs work and what limits their clinical effectiveness.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows how blocking hormonal growth signals can selectively suppress hormone-dependent cancer cells.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how missing cell cycle checkpoints create vulnerabilities that treatments can exploit.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting PARP selectively kills cancer cells that cannot repair the resulting double-strand DNA breaks.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying and inhibiting the activated oncogenic proteins on which tumours depend.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitor resistance and long-term treatment limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why kinase inhibition often controls rather than cures cancer and how treatment must adapt to tumour resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-directed cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognise cancer cell surface proteins to direct therapeutic activity towards those cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic evaluates whether the body's existing immune responses protect against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint blockade and tumour recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade restores antitumour T cell activity and why tumour neoantigens influence its effectiveness.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered approaches that give T cells targeted access to cancer cells rather than relying on naturally occurring tumour recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how matching treatment to individual tumours can address the limitations of cancer therapy.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how prevention and earlier detection contribute to apparent improvements in cancer outcomes.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how future therapeutic progress must be weighed against established survival benefits and patients' quality of life.
